b:
I'd love to let words fall the way Vaali did. But perhaps because I love everything I see, it hasn't stopped at one. I fell in love with Tamil. I still love it. I love nature and the divine. I love everything it is possible to love.

Among the gods you can love Kannan. You can love Kandan. There's no need for any difference of man or woman there. But there are no poems about loving goddesses. Discrimination there too. You can cover it up and call it propriety

It was the poet who gave love its divinity. Once poems grew scarce, cinema became its Shankara Mutt. The love of Bhagavathar's day is something we will never see again. Nobody is going to wait while you sing "I love you" with all the musical flourishes. Then came the heroic love of the MGR era. In one way or another that continues to this day. Part of the reason is the history of human evolution.

It was only in the eighties that love began to widen. With Muthal Mariyathai, Mouna Raagam and the like, society faced new kinds of love. The same showed in the films of the 90s and the early 2000s. Later, as directors understood that there were stories beyond love, love dwindled. Today cinema talks about alpha males and all that. All I can do is write that I'll catch the moon for you. So on behalf of people like me, I boycott it🙊

Who doesn't love the early-morning sun. The pet puppy that comes running with longing. The full moon. The third-day crescent. Thick mist, cold wind, a pouring waterfall: is there anyone who hasn't loved these, even for a moment?

To me, love is a beautiful poem. Even as time passes, a poem's beauty doesn't fade. But if the taste for it fades, the beauty of love grows dim

Love

until time ends
note: Vaali was a much-loved Tamil film lyricist. Kannan (Krishna) and Kandan (Murugan) are gods often addressed as lovers in devotional poetry. A Shankara Mutt is a monastery of the Shankaracharya order, keeper of tradition. M. K. Thyagaraja Bhagavathar and M. G. Ramachandran (MGR) were the great Tamil film heroes of earlier eras; Muthal Mariyathai and Mouna Raagam are celebrated 1980s love stories.
